transcript: Mar del Plata. 17 years old. I wanted to build a games website.
That year, every road opened up. I'm self-taught: I read a lot and study online.
2021 – 2022 · TACH Argentina · Software Developer. Remote development: a virtual wallet, on web and mobile.
2023 – 2024 · Ada ITW · Professor. I taught JavaScript and React.

Since 2024 · Tsoft, for Tuenti and Telefónica: the Tuenti roulette and the referral system (the game came back), automatic top-up and payments. React, React Native, TypeScript, Next.js, Tailwind, Node.js and SQL.
January 2026: Special Recognition from Tsoft. 2026: Dev Ssr → Ssr AI Fullstack Developer.
CompliA: a RAG assistant for Telefónica's compliance portal. I designed and built it. In internal production. (Demo clip, with sample data.)

And my own branches: Eclipse (in development), HandyX (in development · launches Nov 10), Volta (demo), Velmar (demo made for a client), DentalOS (demo), Supernova Eventos (prototype), games-market (test bench), Kinetic Studio (32 trailers in code).

Technologies, by where I used them. At work: React, TypeScript, Next.js, React Native, Tailwind, Node.js, SQL, CI/CD and RAG with an LLM. In my projects: security (HttpOnly cookies, CSRF, 2FA, Argon2), Python, C, motion with GSAP and WebGL, and tests with Vitest and Playwright. Studying: machine learning fundamentals, AWS and Azure.
An agentic system, split into parts: 11 agents with separate roles. Not a prompt: a system with roles.
Specification first, code second. Every claim carries its level of evidence. Gates with human approval. Tested, not eyeballed.
Run of 10/27/2026, all green: Eclipse-Web 463 tests, Eclipse backend 779, internal portal 132 and 14 browser journeys. Nothing ships without human approval.
Ignacio Gauna. Ssr AI Fullstack Developer. I build AI software that ships.
Open to new opportunities. I'm looking for a Ssr or Sr fullstack role with AI. ignaciogauna.developer@gmail.com

method.label: 05 · Method
method.title: How I create value.
method.lead: Six steps. Each with something I did, not a nice phrase.

steps.name: Understand the problem
steps.text: Before building, I understand the context and the business. Talking to the people who use the software changes what gets prioritised.
steps.example: In-person day with clients in Buenos Aires (April 2026): demos, alignment and direct conversation about their real challenges.

steps.name: Align and negotiate priorities
steps.text: I agree on scope and priorities before writing code, and I hold the difficult conversations when they're needed.
steps.example: At Tsoft I take part in technical decisions with the team and support people who join.

steps.name: Design
steps.text: I design the interface and the system together: rules, states and limits before pretty screens.
steps.example: Volta and DentalOS: navigable demos with their own identity and labelled data.

steps.name: Build in stages
steps.text: I split the work into small batches, each with its acceptance criteria.
steps.example: Eclipse moves forward in documented batches, with approval gates.

steps.name: Show and validate
steps.text: I show something that works as early as possible and test it: automated tests, visual QA and demos.
steps.example: Velmar: a navigable demo for a client, with sample data.

steps.name: Deliver and learn
steps.text: I ship with CI/CD, document what I learned and apply it again.
steps.example: At Tsoft I work with deployment pipelines, integrations and CI/CD on Telefónica and Tuenti projects.

method.readsNote: Reading and learning, not certifications. I don't count them as practice until I have an example.
method.cycle: A loop, not a line: what I learn when delivering comes back in as the next problem.

system.label: 06 · System
system.title: An agentic system, split into parts.
system.lead: I code with agents, but each one has its own part and nothing ships without a person who approves.

points.title: Not a prompt: a system with roles
points.text: I built 11 agents with separate responsibilities (product, UX/UI, design, marketing, and frontend, backend, cybersecurity, games and trailer architects), with skills that load depending on the task.

points.title: Specification first, code second
points.text: Every change starts with a short document: problem, scope, acceptance criteria and how to roll back. The work is cut into small batches.

points.title: Every claim carries its level of evidence
points.text: I tell apart what I read, what I tested locally and what runs in a real environment. What I haven't tested is labelled «not tested».

points.title: Gates with human approval
points.text: The agents don't publish, spend or change prices on their own. I authorise publishing and spending.

points.title: Tested, not eyeballed
points.text: The main projects have automated tests, end-to-end tests with Playwright and CI that runs the tests and the build. Run of 10/27/2026, all green: Eclipse-Web 463 tests, Eclipse backend 779 and internal portal 132, plus 14 complete browser journeys.

points.title: Visual QA with binary criteria
points.text: Redesigns are compared against the previous state at several widths and with reduced motion. I state the limits: I test in Chromium.

points.title: Cost and honesty as design rules
points.text: No invented testimonials or clients, everything fictional says «Demo», and no new dependency or spending without my OK.

system.limits: What I don't say: that the agents work on their own, that the system has been audited or that a pentest has been done. The backend's database tests run in CI; I did not run them in the run above.

agents.name: Frontend architect

agents.name: Backend architect
agents.role: Layers, schemas, services and transactions, always discovery first.

agents.name: Cybersecurity
agents.role: Threat modelling, OWASP and hardening; tests only in our own environments.

agents.name: Game architect
agents.role: Mechanics, reward economies and web game performance.

agents.name: Trailer architect
agents.role: Direction, storyboard, motion and sound for pieces like this trailer.

about.label: 08 · About
about.title: From Mar del Plata.
paragraphs: I started studying at 17 with one idea: to build a games website. That site doesn't exist, but it opened the road I'm on.
I'm 100% self-taught: I like to read and study online. I taught JavaScript and React, and today I work as a Ssr AI Fullstack Developer.
I care about what happens between a business problem and a product people actually use.
